results.controlIntent: a. Develop, document, and maintain under configuration control, a current baseline configuration of the system; and b. Review and update the baseline configuration of the system: 1. [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; 2. When required due to [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances]; and 3. When system components are installed or upgraded.

judgment.rationale:
CM-2 requires (a) a documented, configuration-controlled baseline and (b) a defined process for reviewing and updating that baseline periodically, upon defined circumstances, and when components are installed or upgraded.

Combining the two evidence signals retrieved:

1. **Model Registry (id: 6b65ec42-06bf-4b3f-8270-6f2b5ad0d651):** Only a single model package version (v1) exists, approved on 2025-12-01 and created the day before. There is no version history, no evidence of a documented baseline configuration artifact, and no indication of a defined review cadence or update triggers. A single-version registry with no prior versions cannot demonstrate that baseline reviews have occurred or that a configuration-controlled baseline is being maintained over time.

2. **Endpoint Config (id: a0551a81-dd1d-4423-895c-e22fac609dd8):** Data capture is disabled (captureEnabled=false, capturePercentage=0, captureDestination=null) and network isolation is off. The absence of data capture means there is no automated mechanism to detect configuration drift or trigger baseline reviews based on runtime behavior — a gap that undermines the "review when circumstances require" requirement. The instance type (ml.m5.large) is the only concrete configuration parameter documented.

Together, these signals show: no documented baseline configuration artifact, no evidence of a periodic review schedule, no evidence of circumstance-triggered or upgrade-triggered reviews, and no data-capture mechanism to support ongoing configuration monitoring. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No baseline configuration document or IaC artifact (e.g., CloudFormation/Terraform template) was retrievable — human attestation needed to confirm whether one exists outside AWS SageMaker metadata.
No evidence of an organization-defined review frequency policy or schedule (e.g., quarterly review cadence) — requires human attestation from the configuration management team.
No evidence of circumstance-triggered review criteria (CM-2.b.2) — requires policy documentation review.
No evidence of upgrade-triggered baseline reviews (CM-2.b.3) — only one model version exists, so no historical upgrade events are observable.
Data capture is disabled, removing a key observability signal that could support automated drift detection and review triggers; enabling it would strengthen future evidence collection.
Network isolation is off — while not directly a CM-2 gap, it may indicate broader configuration governance gaps worth investigating.
